rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> three-year (2019<U+2013>2021) replicated greenhouse field trial in Yangling, Shaanxi, with CK, farmers'-practice drip fertigation (FP) and intelligent sensor-controlled drip fertigation (IF). Q2: Results 'Ambient temperature and irrigation rates' (Fig. 2) and 'Fruit yield, irrigation water and nutrient use efficiency' (Table 6) <U+2013> sensor-controlled drip fertigation applied 61<U+2013>92 mm vs 97.5<U+2013>136 mm under conventional drip fertigation, saving 29<U+2013>37% of irrigation water, and raised IWUE by 61<U+2013>73% over FP without a significant yield loss; Discussion states IF reduced N, P2O5, K2O by 46%, 72%, 57% while increasing nutrient use efficiency. Q4: Root growth section (Figs. 7<U+2013>8, Table 4) and correlation section (Fig. 9) <U+2013> the study measured root length, surface area, tips and volume, found IF increased fine-root parameters 137<U+2013>232% over FP, and reported significant positive correlations between root indices and IWUE/nutrient use efficiency, proposed as the mechanism; soil water was continuously monitored with FDR sensors to control irrigation.
rows.notes: All three treatments used drip irrigation; the comparison is intelligent sensor-controlled drip fertigation versus conventional drip fertigation, not drip versus another irrigation method. Q2 is answered yes because the passage concerns precise water supply and efficient water/fertilizer use of drip fertigation, which is exactly what the IF treatment demonstrates; but note the saving is attributable to the sensor-based scheduling rather than to drip fertigation per se. Single method (field measurement), one site, one crop (different cultivars per year), plot scale only. Q7: the authors explain the result by the stage-specific soil moisture thresholds and wetting depth having met crop requirements, and mention high cost as an obstacle to adoption, but these are not stated as conditions required for the effect. Q8: no limitations of the result are stated. Q9: no standard deviation or error for the water-saving/IWUE result is visible in the text (tables not reproduced); only across-year ranges are given.

notes: Text lacks tables and figures (only captions/descriptions in prose), and the reference list is absent; dispersion statistics that may appear in Table 6 could not be verified.
